facts.raw_span: a 4-week history of a rapidly growing left caruncular lesion
an amelanotic, pedunculated mass with an ulcerated surface, arising from the caruncle
no evidence of PAM (primary acquired melanosis)
The specimen measured 8 × 6 × 5 mm and had a 4-mm ulceration with necrotic tissue on its surface
Revealed a solid tumor with an inflamed crust on its surface, composed of large anaplastic cells with mitotic activity
Showed positive reactivity to melanocytic markers HMB45, MITF2, and Melan-A
The Ki-67 proliferation marker showed a significant number of cycling cells
Sentinel lymph node biopsy findings were negative
Conjunctival and orbital biopsies revealed no tumor
Ulcerated, pedunculated, caruncular tumor
Mitotically active tumor containing anaplastic epithelioid cells
Melanoma cells showing immunoreactivity for Melan-A

concepts.why: The presence of an amelanotic, pedunculated mass with an ulcerated surface, along with positive reactivity to melanocytic markers and high mitotic activity, supports the diagnosis of Malignant Melanoma of the Caruncle.
The presence of a solid tumor with anaplastic cells, high mitotic activity, and significant Ki-67 proliferation explains the uncovered facts of a rapidly growing and ulcerated caruncular lesion.

rationales.F02: The presence of an amelanotic, pedunculated mass with an ulcerated surface is highly suggestive of a malignant melanoma, particularly in the context of the caruncle.
rationales.F05: The histopathological finding of a solid tumor with an inflamed crust and large anaplastic cells with mitotic activity is characteristic of a malignant melanoma.
rationales.F06: The positive reactivity to melanocytic markers HMB45, MITF2, and Melan-A supports the diagnosis of a melanoma.
rationales.F11: The presence of mitotically active tumor cells with anaplastic epithelioid morphology is indicative of a malignant process, consistent with melanoma.
rationales.F12: The immunoreactivity of melanoma cells to Melan-A further supports the diagnosis of a melanoma.

frontier_selector.why: The presence of an amelanotic, pedunculated mass with an ulcerated surface, arising from the caruncle, along with positive reactivity to melanocytic markers and immunoreactivity for Melan-A, decided it.
